newsitem.title: ITALY: Moderate earthquake shakes northern Italy.
newsitem.headline: Moderate earthquake shakes northern Italy.

text.p: A moderate earthquake registering 4.8 on the Richter scale was felt across northern Italy on Tuesday but there were no immediate reports of damage or casualties.
The tremor, at 11:56 a.m. (0956 GMT), had its epicentre in the northern region of Emilia Romagna, the National Geophysics Institute said.
It was felt as far south as Florence and in all areas of the north including Milan, Bolzano in the eastern Italian Dolomites and Genoa on the western coast.
State railways said they had suspended services between Bologna and Milan as a precautionary measure to check the safety of bridges following the tremor.
Fire department helicopters were flying over the area to survey for damage, civil authorities said.

In Mantua near the earthquake's epicentre, many people frightened by the tremor ran into the streets. Firefighters in the historic town were checking the safety of buildings, especially those several hundred years old.
